lessons.keep: Use a stable example and one highlighted change to explain precise editing.
lessons.avoid: Using waveform graphics as a substitute for demonstrating the actual editing control.
lessons.open: Audible voice quality, accent fidelity, editing smoothness, benchmark validity and integration steps remain unverified.
try: For Tin, show one campaign sentence with only a selected product or audience detail changed, then its approved result.
Place a brief input-and-control demonstration before the charts so viewers know how the voice model is used.

comparison.story: Introduce the company and new model. → Present preference-test claims. → Argue for speed in model and production use. → Give a pronunciation example for critical information. → Present expressive and cloning examples. → Illustrate a voice-change comparison. → Isolate the intended content edit. → Describe infrastructure and device reach. → Finish with an assistant-style handoff and destination.
